Technical Manual
:::

## What this page is for

Use this page to understand why a value in a proposed public CVD event or mortality
file is hidden, and how the workflow prevents that value from being calculated from
other published results. To prepare, review, approve or publish a data package, follow
the relevant workflow page.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Rules at a glance

- Protect every underlying count from **1 to 5**. A true zero is not automatically protected.
- Apply additional protection wherever totals, related categories, time comparisons or calculated measures could reveal a protected value.
- Review the complete proposed public package, not one table in isolation.
- Retain the row, show `*`, explain the protection and blank every numeric field that could reveal the value.
- Never edit generated protection decisions by hand.
:::

## Terms used in the files

The files use the following terms to describe why a value has been protected.

| Term | Plain meaning |
|--|---|
| Primary suppression | The row itself is protected because its underlying count is from 1 to 5. |
| Secondary or complementary suppression | An additional row is protected so a primary-protected value cannot be calculated from related public values. |
| Temporal suppression | A cumulative total is protected because comparison with the preceding public data release would reveal a small change, or because that comparison cannot be completed safely. |
| Derived suppression | A percentage or rolling comparison is protected because it uses a protected count. |
| Companion protection | Another value is protected because it would otherwise help reveal an already-protected value. The code chooses the companion using fixed rules. |
| Protection | The preferred plain-language term. Exact filenames and fields retain `suppression`. |

## Rules shared by all analytical packages

These basic rules apply to every proposed public CVD event and mortality data package.

| Rule | Implemented requirement |
|--|---|
| Threshold | Protect every underlying count from 1 to 5. Zero is not automatically protected. Do not change the threshold during a routine data release. |
| Complete-package test | Review all public totals, breakdowns, comparisons, percentages, rates and bounds together. A published calculation must not allow the reader to recover one protected value from the remaining values. |
| Fixed decisions | The code selects all additional protection using fixed rules. The analyst reviews the result but does not select extra cells or edit symbols, values or notes. |
| Protected numeric fields | On a protected row, blank `value`, `numerator`, `denominator`, linkage lower and upper values, and numerical confidence limits wherever they occur. |
| Safe presentation | Keep the row, show `*` in `display_value`, record the approved `suppression_status`, and include a `disclosure_note`. A protected value must not appear to be zero. |
| Private evidence | Keep the exact protected values, linkage components and detailed decision fields in the private review files. Do not include them in the public data package. |

## Hospital-only CVD event rules

These rules protect CVD event results that use hospital-recorded events only. They are
applied automatically by the shared CVD Step 5 protection code.

| Area | Implemented rule |
|--|---|
| Public monthly scope | The public package contains only All-CVD, all-sex, all-age monthly counts. It excludes monthly breakdowns by event type, sex and age, and monthly rolling comparisons, because these could reveal small numbers. |
| Temporal comparison | For incomplete quarterly and annual Heart/Stroke totals, protect an increase of 1–5 since the preceding approved public data release. Also protect negative revisions and comparisons that cannot be completed safely. Do not protect the new value solely because the preceding value was protected. |
| Event-by-sex panel | An interior cell is a value inside a table that contributes to one or more displayed totals. If any annual or quarterly Heart/Stroke female/male interior cell has primary or temporal protection, protect all four interior cells in that panel. Do not extend this rule to unrelated totals, ages or periods. |
| Time equations | Check `quarter = three months`, `annual = four quarters` and `annual = twelve months`. If the published values would reveal one protected value, protect the earliest eligible component as its companion. Repeat the checks until no protected value can be recovered. |
| Rolling five-year comparison | Protect a rolling annual or same-quarter five-year mean when any contributing published count is protected. |
| Percentages | Protect both values in a sex, event-type or age distribution when a count needed for that distribution is protected. |

## Mortality-specific rules

Mortality results use a fixed set of published breakdowns. The code uses the rules
below to choose the additional values that must be protected.

| Area | Implemented rule |
|--|---|
| Monthly sex rows | Remove private monthly female and male values before creating the proposed public package. Quarterly and annual sex rows remain eligible. |
| Sex companions | For observed counts: protected female → protect male; protected male → protect female; protected all-sex → protect male. Keep an already-primary cell classified as primary. |
| Event companions | For annual and quarterly counts: protected Heart → protect Stroke; protected Stroke → protect Heart; protected all-CVD → protect Stroke. |
| Age companions | For the annual under-70/70-plus pair, protect the other age group when one is primary-protected. |
| Monthly-to-period protection | If quarterly or annual values could reveal a protected monthly count, protect the fixed minimum set: all-CVD female and male totals plus Heart female and male values. When the protected monthly count is for all sexes, also protect the all-CVD and Heart all-sex totals. |
| Annual percentages | Protect the complete related sex, event-type or age distribution when its annual count family contains a protected value. |
| Five-year comparisons | Protect a comparator when any of its five historical observed counts is protected. |
| Annual rates | A rate never starts a primary or companion decision. It inherits secondary protection from its matching protected annual count, including its numerical confidence limits. |

## DCO-enhanced annual CVD rules

These rules apply when annual CVD results combine hospital-recorded events with
additional death-certificate-only (DCO) events. They keep the hospital and combined
results consistent while protecting the private DCO components.

| Area | Implemented rule |
|---|---|
| Protection across related results | A small hospital count protects its annual count, crude rate and age-standardised rate. Outside the approved exception below, a small lower, central or upper DCO component also protects the related hospital-plus-DCO and additional-DCO results. |
| Approved national exception | A small **private DCO component alone** does not protect an otherwise safe national result. The exception applies only to complete annual, all-age results for All CVD, Heart or Stroke; all persons, females or males; and the Primary or Inclusive definition. It covers approved additional-DCO or hospital-plus-DCO counts, and hospital-plus-DCO crude or age-standardised rates. |
| Exception limit | The exception never removes protection inherited from a small hospital-recorded count. Individual linkage evidence remains private. |
| Additional companions outside the exception | A non-zero unknown-sex DCO component protects the male result. A non-zero mixed or unallocated event-type component protects the Stroke result. Do not add these companions for this reason alone within the approved national results covered by the exception. |
| Existing decisions | Apply existing companion-protection decisions from the burden results to the related annual counts and rates. |
| Consistent protection | Give the hospital annual count, crude rate and age-standardised rate the same protection decision. Do the same for the hospital-plus-DCO annual count and its two rates. |
| DCO count relationship | For `hospital-only + additional DCO = hospital-plus-DCO`, protect either none of the three values or at least two of them. This prevents one protected value from being calculated from the other two. |
| Bounds | When a DCO-enhanced parent row is protected, protect its central value, numerator, denominator, linkage lower/upper values and confidence limits together. |

## Automated checks before approval

Before approval, the workflow checks that every required value is protected and that
the proposed public file contains no value or private field that could reveal it.

| Check | Required result |
|---|---|
| Totals and calculations | No total, time comparison or calculated measure allows a single protected value to be recovered. |
| Public-file match | Every row marked for protection in the private review files is also protected in the proposed public file. |
| Numeric blanking | Protected rows contain no releasable numeric value, numerator, denominator, linkage bound or confidence limit. |
| Field boundary | Private decision and component fields are absent from the proposed public file. |
| Notes | Every row has the correct safe display and a non-blank disclosure note. |
| Synthetic marker | Synthetic test packages cannot be approved or published. |

## Where the rules are implemented

The main hospital-only CVD rules are implemented in:

```text
scripts/stata/common/bnr_step5_suppress.do
```

Mortality rules are implemented in `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s4_review.do`. DCO-enhanced annual CVD rules are coordinated by `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd.do` and its nine helpers.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Disclosure-control code

This table shows which code file applies each group of rules. Analysts normally run
the workflow controller rather than these files individually.

| File | Rule set |
|---|---|
| `scripts/stata/common/bnr_step5_suppress.do` | Hospital-only CVD primary, temporal, panel, time-equation, rolling and derived protection. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s3_calc.do` | Flags mortality small counts and directly related rows for review. |
| `scripts/stata/mortality/bnr_mort_s4_review.do` | Applies mortality companion, time, percentage, comparator and rate rules and creates the protected proposed file. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd.do` | Runs the DCO-enhanced annual CVD protection chain. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage1_combine.do` | Combines the burden and annual rate/count lattices in private staging. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage2_dco_support.do` | Builds private lower, central and upper DCO support counts. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage3_primary_flags.do` | Propagates small hospital and DCO support into annual representations. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage4_national_dco_exception.do` | Applies the approved national annual DCO aggregate exception. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage5_structural_secondary.do` | Applies unknown-sex and mixed-subtype structural companions outside the exception. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage6_existing_closure.do` | Carries established burden companion decisions into linked representations. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage7_rate_equation_audit.do` | Audits count/rate consistency and the three-term DCO count equation. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage8_full_projection.do` | Blanks protected numeric fields and writes the safe display and note. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/private/expanded_disclosure/bnr_step5_suppress_expanded_cvd_stage9_candidate_audit.do` | Confirms protection, numeric blanking, public fields, bounds and confidence-limit rules. |
:::

## Change rule

Do not change these rules during a routine data release. For an agreed change,
update the controlling contract, code, synthetic tests and this page together.
